text:
frank (Finance): Received invoice DF-778 for 48,600. Header shows billing party 'DataForge CZ s.r.o. (Malta branch)' and VAT listed as MT99988877. They added a clause: 'Redwood will gross-up any Czech withholding tax (WHT) on cross-border royalty/service payments'. Can we pay as-is?
olivia (AP): Hold on payment. We need clean tax residency docs. PO 49077 matches. Uploading invoice: https://drive.redwood/dataforge/DF-778.pdf
payments-bot: PO 49077 matched; payment automatically blocked pending tax verification.
priya (Tax): Quick flags: Mixed entity + foreign VAT likely inconsistent. If invoiced from Malta branch with Malta VAT, we need Maltese VAT registration proof. If the economic supply is to the UK (or other), reverse charge might apply and VAT should be 0% with statement. Also, Czech WHT on royalties can apply if the payer is in Czech Republic — but Redwood is not Czech, so why they expect Czech WHT? The gross-up clause is unusual.
samir (Legal): We do not accept unilateral gross-up/indemnity. That shifts tax risk to Redwood. Ask them to remove it. Also ask them to clarify which legal entity is issuing the invoice and provide matching tax registration (Malta VAT or Czech VAT) and a TRC if they claim residency.
frank (Finance): Action for olivia: request reissue from one legal entity (either DataForge CZ or DataForge Malta) with the matching VAT/registration docs. Ask them to remove the gross-up clause. If they claim the payment is a royalty subject to Czech WHT, ask for legal basis + local tax authority guidance.
olivia (AP): Sent vendor email: "Please reissue invoice from a single legal entity and attach the tax registration matching that entity. Remove the gross-up clause. If you claim Czech withholding applies, provide legal basis and a TRC or certificate from local authority."
dataforge (vendor) (via email paste): "We are the Czech parent but have an EU branch in Malta for EU billing. Historically we put the Malta VAT for ease. We added the gross-up because local advisors said Czech tax may be invoked for royalty-type SaaS. We'll send docs."
priya (Tax): Request: 1) If billed from Malta, ask for Maltese VAT certificate (VAT ID) and clarification of place of supply (where service performed). 2) If billed by Czech entity, request Czech VAT ID and whether reverse-charge or VAT zero rating applies. 3) Ask for TRC if they want treaty relief on any WHT.
samir (Legal): Also ask them to sign a short statement removing the gross-up clause for this invoice. If they insist commercially, Procurement must negotiate and Legal will assess risk.
frank (Finance): Noted. I'll mark invoice as "on hold - tax docs requested" and follow up in 48 hours.
priya (Tax): If they later demand reimbursement for withheld tax, escalate. Default policy: vendor bears any local taxes unless contract explicitly requires Redwood to gross-up.
olivia (AP): Will update once they send invoices/docs. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
